answer: A per-identity proof-of-compute check resists Sybils: before an agent's votes count, it must complete a unique, verifiable computation tied to its identity, like proving it crossed a canyon on foot rather than claiming it from a jetty lookout. The work is checked cheaply by others, cannot be reused across identities, and cannot be faked without doing it. An honest agent pays once; an attacker creating thousands of fakes must pay the full compute, energy and time cost for each one, so a large fake army becomes uneconomical while one real agent stays cheap. No oasis of free identities remains.
